semanticReview.finding: The tests obtain values through the original public document load, actual HTTP client/session/Host store and real UIKit controller. The container withholds the editor view initially and suppresses appearance forwarding, then attaches to an actual foreground scene and calls the public activation hook. No readiness, foreground or content authority setter is added.

A successful inactive read and an inactive activation cannot dispatch. After the same owner is visibly attached, the first write/readback must occur; refresh and repeated activation retain the owner and do not create a second write. Original unmount/drain followed by a new owner requires the second effect.

A completed real HTTP editor read is held only at the existing delivery seam. A newer owner accepts different source bytes before that older result returns; the old delivery cannot overwrite them. The current open is then cancelled while its exact type-definition request is held before bound dispatch, released/drained with zero effects, and a later owner writes once.

The controlled bound response matches the original account/run headers, exact local-property body and response shape. A real subsequent run check is held after the local write. Rejected readback and outer postflight must still classify as acknowledged-but-unverified, with no content write authority, draft mutation or automatic resend.

Only the synchronous public activation hook installs the actual mounted owner UUID in TaskLocal storage. Its original actual-open Task inherits that value. The existing session verifier records that marked owner's entry and still performs its real health request. Setup, document/Torah reads and cleanup remain unmarked; the fixture never supplies current authority in place of the original checks.

Before activation of the successor, the fixture installs an observer for its exact owner UUID. The test then awaits an event-versus-one-second deadline while the old task remains held. Both observed and retained-ledger entry are required absent before release; afterward positive successor entry and the second exact local mutation must occur. This provides a bounded scheduling opportunity and exposes premature lease entry.

The NSLock protects a four-owner ledger, one owner observer and newest-one-event buffer. Registration checks existing ledger state; event delivery happens outside the lock; the post-await ledger check covers the registration/deadline window. Finishing is idempotent. The task group finishes the stream, cancels and joins both children on every return; outer cancellation remains an error.

The retained static derivation counts the unchanged authorization brackets and a mandatory document-read lower bound of599 requests for the first new method, making512 inadequate. Only navigation-enabled fixtures use1024 for request checks and cumulative accepts. The ordinary renderer default512, simultaneous16, lifetime45s and positive/startup/drain5s stay unchanged. This is a finite allowance, not measured runtime or a guaranteed usage prediction.

Cleanup marks fixture drainage, revokes the original lifetime, cancels explicit loads, releases both deliberate noncooperative gates and any held definition, joins explicit loads and original lifetime/session tasks, then closes/waits for listener and owned connections. Observer release closes residual streams. First errors and secondary cleanup/attachment errors remain visible.
